description: An eight-stage sequencer with two knobs a stage, a gate output and a select input for each stage, and outputs for either row, their difference, the smaller, the larger and the stage as a pitch

params.text: Sets the voltage row A gives at that stage, 0V to 5V
Sets the voltage row B gives at that stage, 0V to 5V
Jumps to that stage and holds it while it is pressed, and makes it the stage the PRESET input recalls
Switches the CLOCK input on and off; with it down the clock input does nothing
Switches the V.CLOCK input on and off; with it down the vertical clock does nothing

inputs.text: Jumps to that stage and holds it while the voltage is above 1.8V, and makes it the stage the PRESET input recalls
Jumps to the first stage on each rise past 1.8V, ahead of every other way of choosing a stage
Jumps to the stage last chosen by a select button or select input, on each rise past 1.8V
Holds the current stage while the voltage is above 1.8V, so the clock is ignored
Reverses the direction the sequence steps in, on each rise past 1.8V
Advances one stage on each rise past 1.8V, while its enable switch is on
Moves the A or B output between the two rows on each rise past 1.8V, while its enable switch is on

outputs.text: 5V while that stage is the current one, and 0V otherwise
5V while any stage is being held by a select button or select input, and 0V otherwise
Row A's knob for the current stage, 0V to 5V
Row B's knob for the current stage, 0V to 5V
Row A's voltage less row B's for the current stage, -5V to +5V
Whichever of the two rows is lower at the current stage, 0V to 5V
Whichever of the two rows is higher at the current stage, 0V to 5V
The stage number as a voltage, 0V to 1.34V in whole-tone steps, made to be patched as a pitch
Row A or row B for the current stage, whichever the vertical clock last chose

notes: both enable switches come up off, so a fresh module ignores CLOCK and V.CLOCK until they are switched on
when more than one thing calls for a stage at once, RESET wins, then the select buttons, select inputs and PRESET together, then HOLD, and CLOCK last
with two select inputs high at the same time the lower-numbered stage wins
patch a stage gate output into RESET, PRESET, a select input, DIRECTION or V.CLOCK to make the eight stages into a shorter, longer or swinging sequence
